recommendation: Have FHIR-I and the build tooling owner decide the policy/tooling path. If FHIR-13482's restored ImplementationGuide defaults remain intentional, add generated separate defaultValue and meaningWhenMissing lists and update the ElementDefinition narrative. If FHIR-15121 should prevail, remove the resource defaults and keep FHIR-13337 satisfied by the no-defaults outcome.
issue_request: FHIR-13337 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-I issue asking that ElementDefinition's Missing Elements page split the combined default-values and meaningWhenMissing list into two lists. Its later Jira comment said the change was no longer needed after default values had been removed.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentions FHIR-13337. Historical commits dd83fb1f2ac73c98af6be086bb76b925c37b1f4e and 72143f2fd3d86e1d1de43b7aab6821463d9611ab removed default values and default examples from ElementDefinition source, matching the Jira comment's no-action rationale rather than implementing a separate generated list.
additional_context: FHIR-15121 and FHIR-13482 are tightly related and already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-15121 records the broader policy against defaultValue[x] in FHIR resources, while FHIR-13482 restores defaultValueBoolean=false on current ImplementationGuide isExample successor fields. ElementDefinition still has only one missing-element-list placeholder, and the STU3 rendered page shows that placeholder historically emitted default values and meaningWhenMissing entries together.
reconciliation: No source change was made. A safe fix would require either generator/template support for separate defaultValue and meaningWhenMissing lists while keeping the restored FHIR-13482 defaults, or a work-group decision that the FHIR-15121 no-FHIR-resource-default policy overrides those defaults. A static hand-written source list would risk drift and possible generated-output duplication.
